description: Issue #839 AC1, with ARITY as the discriminating variable: the two declarations of `scale` take one and two parameters, and the call `scale 1 2` matches only the LATER one. A last-wins override would run and print `2`; a first-wins rule would reach `ol-too-many-inputs`; the ruling's rule reports `ol-duplicate-definition` at the second declaration and runs nothing. A fixture whose two definitions were identical would pass under all three, which is why this one varies what the rule turns on. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`.
